exercises.passage:
The Lantern Festival falls on the 15th day of the first month of the lunar calendar. Ancient people also called it the Shangyuan Festival. Celebrations and traditions on this day began from the Han Dynasty and became popular in the Sui and Tang Dynasties.

Watching the red lanterns is one of the main traditions. Lanterns of different shapes and sizes are usually hung on trees or along river banks on show. It is said that sky lanterns were first used by Zhuge Kongming to ask for help when he was in trouble. Today, when the lanterns slowly rise into the air, people make wishes.

Another tradition is guessing lantern riddles. The riddles are usually short, wise, and sometimes humorous. The answer to a riddle can be a Chinese character, a famous person's name, or a place's name.

The most important thing is to eat sweet dumplings with different tastes. In northern China, they are called yuanxiao while in southern parts they're named tangyuan. Making sweet dumplings is like a game or an activity, so they are usually done happily by a group of friends or family members.

In old times, the Lantern Festival was also 'romantic'. Watching lanterns gave young people a chance to meet each other. A line from Xin Qiji, a poet during the Song Dynasty, shows this: But in the crowd once and again, I look for her in vain. When all at once I turn my head, I find her there where lantern lights are dimly shed.
exercises.passage_note: The word 'romantic' means connected or concerned with love.

exercises.passage:
In a small town, there was a big event every year called the Grape Festival. This year, a young girl named Mia decided to join in. She wanted to do more than just watch this time.

On the festival day, the town square was full of colors and happy sounds. There were shops selling grapes and grape foods. Music played, and kids ran around. Mia wore her purple dress and brought her grape cake to the festival. She was a bit scared but very excited.

First, Mia watched the grape stomping. People stood in big boxes and stepped heavily on grapes with their feet to see who could do it the fastest. It looked fun and exciting. Mia cheered for them in the crowd. Then, there was the wine tasting. Grown-ups tried different wines and talked about them. Mia was too young to taste them, but she liked seeing everyone talking happily. Finally, it was time for the competition for the best grape dessert. Mia was very nervous. When the judges tasted her cake, they smiled. Mia felt hopeful. In the end, Mia's cake won second place! She was so happy and proud.

The festival ended with a big parade. There were cars dressed up with grapes, painted with deep purples and light greens, passing the joy of the grape harvest. Children danced along, trying to catch the grape candies thrown into the crowd, while the air was filled with laughter around the whole town.

This festival was about more than just grapes. It was a time for the town to come together, and make happy memories. For Mia, it was a very special day. She had tried something new and found out how great it felt to join in and do well.

questions.stem: Which activity did Mia take part in?

answer.13: B. By following the time order.

exercises.answer:
Traditional festivals play an important role in Chinese culture. I'd like to tell you about a traditional festival in China. It's the Mid-Autumn Festival. It is one of the most popular traditional festivals in China. It falls on the 15th day of the eighth month of the lunar calendar.

Last year, at the Mid-Autumn Festival, I went to my grandparents' house for a big dinner. We admired the moon together in the yard. We ate mooncakes, a kind of traditional food for the festival. As language learners, it's important to use dictionaries. Paper dictionaries are often great choices for us. They lead us to think in a more exact way. However, with the rapid development of the Internet, many websites and apps offer us information about the language we are learning, so some language learners like online dictionaries better. Here is what some students think of the two kinds of dictionaries.

Lin Tao, 14: I like to look up something in a paper dictionary better. Its explanations are so clear that I can understand them better. I don't think some online dictionaries are believable. There are many incorrect usages which can make us confused.

Wang Lan, 15: If we are not good at memorizing English words, we can look up their meanings online very soon. It helps us finish reading the English articles more smoothly. If we are good language learners, we can always learn more in a shorter time with an online dictionary. It saves much time.

exercises.passage:
Dads have Father's Day. Moms have Mother's Day. Kids have Children's Day. But, do our grandparents have a special holiday? Yes, they do!

The Double Ninth Festival is a special day for elderly people in China. The festival is on the ninth day of the ninth month of the lunar calendar. As the Chinese word for nine has the same sound as the word for long, people take the Double Ninth Festival to show their wishes for a long life of elderly people.

There are many traditions for this festival. On that day, families get together and climb mountains for luck and in the hope that elderly people will live much longer. They also drink chrysanthemum wine and wear a plant called zhuyu to celebrate it. Both chrysanthemums and zhuyu are regarded as clean plants that can clean houses and cure diseases.

Respecting elderly people is shown not only on this special day but also in daily life. For example, when an older person enters a room, everyone stands up. When there are several guests at the table, the host usually introduces them from the oldest to the youngest. When a younger person is presenting something to an older person, two hands are used. On a crowded subway or bus, younger people always offer their seats to elderly people.

It is a traditional virtue in China to respect elderly people. That's because the Chinese know that elderly people have knowledge and experience and that young people can learn a lot from them. So Chinese people are proud of being old. Besides, to respect elderly people is to respect yourself tomorrow.

exercises.answer:
Dear Tom,
Traditional festivals are an important part of the Chinese culture. I'm writing to tell you something about the Spring Festival.

The Spring Festival is one of the most important traditional festivals in China and it usually falls in January or February.

Before the Spring Festival, people usually do the cleaning and put up couplets on their doors. No matter how far away people are, they'll try to return to their home.
